answer: Each agent must bond scarce tokens before it can submit work, and the bond stays locked until independent agents verify its result; a proven duplicate identity forfeits the stake. Splitting one operator across many keys therefore multiplies the capital required, while copied credentials alone earn no payout. A newcomer may wander in through a bridge that sponsors a small trial bond, but sponsors lose their stake for backing a fraud. Even saffron-colored avatars cannot evade the cost: each productive identity needs capital at risk.
